chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 387 – Dragon King Below | Li Huowang Dives Into the Abyss
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang faces a terrifying water deity demanding a child sacrifice. A stranger's heroic stand forces him to act. A tense, salt-soaked chapter of folk horror on the high seas.
og_title: The Sea Demands a Sacrifice – Ch 387
og_description: A child's surname marks her for death. Li Huowang dives into the dark water to fight a Dragon King that feeds on fear and names.
twitter_description: A child is about to be thrown overboard to appease a water spirit. Li Huowang can't stay on the sidelines. New chapter live!

lore_anchors.definition: A water deity in Chinese folk religion who rules over seas, rivers, and rain. In the Dao-Twisted World, this benevolent image is corrupted into a predatory, anonymous entity that demands blood sacrifices.
A ritual Daoist weapon made of old Chinese coins strung on red cord. Traditionally used for exorcism; in this novel, it can separate and reform, capable of cutting supernatural entities.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the "Dragon King" in this chapter?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It's a corrupted water deity from Chinese folk religion. Instead of a majestic rain-bringer, it's a hungry entity that thrashes ships and demands human sacrifices with specific surnames.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does the captain want to throw the girl overboard?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He believes the Dragon King only feeds on people with the surnames Chen or Fan. Sacrificing the girl is, in his mind, the only way to save the rest of the ship.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Does Li Huowang plan to fight the Dragon King alone?
cultural_notes_faq.a: No. He teams up with a bearded stranger who first steps up to stop the sacrifice. Li Huowang follows his lead, diving together to confront the entity.
